written: 2026-10-01, after the first dev128 pass (INT8 point estimates of the one-at-a-time arms and the ladder, no intervals yet) and before any 1k measurement, any sentinel format and the freeze
what_was_seen: Empirical bias correction is harmful on the detector: cum5 39.25 -> cum6 28.05 mAP50-95 on dev128, and 0.03 when applied alone to v1 max-abs. The per-channel residual after correction is about 1e-7, so the step does what it is defined to do.
amendments: Freeze rule, clause 'a classifier-default switch is not dropped on detector evidence' is replaced by the rule the classifier study itself used (b2-baseline-repair-protocol-v1, stage S2): a classifier-default switch is dropped only if its leave-one-out arm is better on dev128 with a paired 95 percent interval excluding zero.

Because bias correction is step 6 of the ladder, the two later steps (concatenation pass-through, fused SiLU), the leave-one-out arms, the head put-back arms and the residual diagnostics are also run on the base without bias correction (cum5). The arms are registered in tools/experiment_b2_det/arms2.py. The tests for the contract-changing options (more than 0.5 point with an interval excluding zero on dev128) are evaluated on that base.
The originally registered arms with bias correction stay in the tables as measured.
unchanged: data, panels, metric, statistics, tie rules, regression, sentinel list, storage, the 64 bias-correction images, the 0.5-point test for contract-changing options, and the exit test
